results.notes: X1: one line from a .lua file source, then the script ends; the smallest bind / lease / release path of Lua
results.methodology: Same-process runs of real plugin engine scripts (docs/memory-phase2/ROADMAP.md T1-T4), the method of the first gate: engines and ScriptRuntime are tracked from EngineLifecycleCallback through weak references, and so are the host-side bridge session objects that BridgeExecutionObserver reports at creation (T1 (a)). After every run the runner collects and polls up to pollMs (1 s once 3 runs stayed reachable); a final collection decides 'retained'. Heap deltas compare the sample after the last warm-up with the final sample; thread, Rhino context, engine and bridge registry deltas compare with the sample before the first run (the plugin probe already bound the plugin), bridge threads with the end of the warm-ups (idle workers of the host's cached binder-call pool get up to 65 s to expire first). Bridge registries must return to the start except the connection pools of the Node, Bun and QuickJS clients, which may keep one idle connection each; system-side connections of this process to the plugin package of the scenario (LoadedApk.mServices, hidden_api_policy 1) may be one above the start. Plugin process PSS is recorded after the second measured run and at the end, never judged (R9); for Bun it includes the bun child processes (same uid). Bun and QuickJS report their broker and output callback through BridgeExecutionScope (T6, since P2.2); in addition their host-side session classes (broker, output callback, automation bridge, call executor, provider) are counted through VMDebug.countInstancesOfClasses after every run and must return to the count before the first run; their gate lines are read from the global console by a per-run marker. Lua and Python (P3) run .lua / .py file sources from the working directory (Lua modules in <entry>.modules/); their session classes (Lua: host broker, execution callback, remote session, acquired provider; Python: broker, execution callback, execution, binding) are counted the same way and their gate lines come from the global console by marker. The Python plugin retires its process after every session, so its PSS is often absent at the end. Force mode waits for gateReady(), sleeps forceDelayMs and calls forceStop on every live engine of the run on the main thread.
